analysis.model_thesis: Receiving states adopting externally supplied infrastructure, standards, training pipelines, institutions, and governance vocabulary gain capability while accumulating layer-specific switching costs. Multi-alignment is valuable only if those layers remain genuinely substitutable.
analysis.capability: Observe new domestic compute access, deployed services, locally trained engineers and regulators, and institutions able to execute policy as dated, sourced events.
analysis.dependency: Track hardware and cloud lock-in, maintenance contracts, standards conformity, vendor-specific personnel pipelines, imported institutional templates, and governance vocabulary separately.
analysis.optionality: Infer option space from revealed substitutability: parallel operating stacks, rotating procurement, credible open-source exit ramps, and the practical compatibility of commitments.
analysis.strongest_counterargument: AI software may be less path-dependent than railway or telecommunications infrastructure because APIs, open weights, containers, and transferable skills make several layers near-commodity.
missing_evidence: Longitudinal attempted stack switches with documented cost, duration, and outcome
Evidence of personnel skill transfer across stacks
Evidence that governance vocabulary changed a concrete regulatory or procurement outcome
analysis.falsifier: The thesis is weakened if deep single-supplier adopters switch quickly and cheaply and multi-aligned states show no greater revealed procurement, regulatory, or model-substitution flexibility.
